items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
A stranger texts you: get paid just for liking videos. And the first payment is real.
Narrator
The US regulator, the F T C, calls this a task scam.
Narrator
You like videos or rate products, in sets of forty, and an app shows your earnings climbing.
Narrator
You withdraw a few dollars. It works.
Chars
[smug, deep, rich gold bar, very pleased with himself] See? Easy money. Now, just a tiny deposit.
Narrator
Then a "double task" appears. To unlock it, you must deposit your own money, usually in crypto.
Narrator
Each level asks for more. The balance on screen keeps growing, but it was never real.
Narrator
Reports jumped from about five thousand in all of twenty twenty-three to about twenty thousand in just the first half of twenty twenty-four.
Narrator
The Better Business Bureau says the typical task-scam victim lost about two thousand three hundred dollars in twenty twenty-five.
Narrator
That's the mirage: the first few dollars are bait for your deposit.
Narrator
The F T C's rule is simple: never pay to get paid.
Chars
[nervous, squeaky, high-pitched] So the job was paying me with my own money?
Narrator
Comment: have you ever got a text like this?
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
